text:
A tracheostomy is most often used to provide a reliable airway and to support breathing for patients who need long-term ventilation, such as after prolonged mechanical ventilation or when upper airway obstruction or an inability to protect the airway makes intubation impractical. Of the two options in the team note, the correct one is "As an aid to weaning patients from a ventilator," because a tracheostomy is a common way to help patients come off a ventilator. Repairing vocal cords after paralysis is not a purpose of the procedure.

CONFIDENCE: 85
